note: Written after calibration (SPEC §10.1) and BEFORE the first measured ladder rung. Directions 1-6 are SPEC §11's, 8 is the user's; numeric ranges are computed from the calibration object below (arithmetic in each note). Entry 7 is not a prediction: it records both verdict rules before measurement.

predictions.claim: SBX is bound by CPU. Resident ∞ is bound by memory.
predictions.metric: record.json `binding` and the failed §8 condition at each arm's first failed default-point rung (SBX: host CPU busy ≥ 90% or pace/latency failing with MemAvailable well above the floor; resident ∞: memory_floor, a host-memory/memory-budget refusal or an OOM kill)
predictions.falsifiedBy: SBX's first failed rung bound by memory (memory_floor, host-memory refusal or OOM), or resident ∞'s first failed rung failing on pace/latency with binding=cpu while MemAvailable stays above floor + 1 GiB
predictions.note: Direction fixed by SPEC §11. Calibration: SBX at N=8 uses 3.938 core-s per call; resident VMs grow to a median 74.07 MiB (max 178.4) at N=8. CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: resident ∞'s CPU bound (N ≈ [49.32, 55.49]) is below its memory bound (N ≈ [51.41, 123.8]), so calibration expects resident ∞ to be CPU-bound too; the resident half of this prediction is expected to be falsified.

predictions.claim: SBX holds more sessions than resident ∞ at the default point. Predicted ranges: SBX N_max in [40, 48]; resident ∞ N_max in [48, 48].
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max (SPEC §8, class-matched condition 4, primary rule) per arm, default point
predictions.falsifiedBy: n_max(SBX) ≤ n_max(resident ∞); separately, either arm's n_max outside its range falsifies the numeric part
predictions.note: SBX: cores/session = c × r = 3.938 core-s/call × 0.01744 calls/s = 0.06869 cores; usable = 4 vCPU × [0.80, 0.90] = [3.2, 3.6]; N = [46.59, 52.41] → ladder [40, 48]. Resident ∞: memory: usable = MemAvailable at t0 1.173e+04 MiB − 1536 floor − 1024 headroom = 9170 MiB, N_mem = usable / footprint ∈ [9170 / 178.4 max, 9170 / 74.07 median] = [51.41, 123.8]; CPU: its own measured 3.72 core-s/call × 0.01744 calls/s, N_cpu = [49.32, 55.49]; N = min(N_mem, N_cpu) = [49.32, 55.49] → ladder [48, 48]. CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: the two ranges overlap -- both arms meet the same CPU wall within 0.2184 core-s/call of each other (SBX − resident at N=8; direct lifecycle bench 0.09911 core-s/Exec), and resident ∞'s memory bound is not the tighter one. The direction is SPEC §11's and is not changed; calibration suggests it may be falsified or tie.

predictions.claim: Resident 300 s comes within one ladder step of SBX, in either direction. Predicted range: resident 300 s N_max in [48, 48].
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max, resident 300 s vs SBX, default point; ladder index difference
predictions.note: Memory: usable / (median footprint × held share) = 9170 / (74.07 × 0.5611) = 220.7. CPU: the resident per-call CPU measured at N=8 (3.72 core-s/call; resident 300 s runs the same commands on a resident VM), N = [49.32, 55.49]. N = min(memory, CPU) = [49.32, 55.49] → ladder [48, 48]. Cold wakes (2.3/session-hour) are not costed; each costs about one lifecycle (direct bench 0.09911 core-s), so they lower the CPU bound by well under 1%.

predictions.claim: Longer gaps help SBX and resident 300 s, not resident ∞. At H = 7200 s, SBX's and resident 300 s's N_max rise; resident ∞ stays within one ladder step of its default.
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max at the long point vs the default point, per arm
predictions.falsifiedBy: SBX or resident 300 s n_max at H=7200 not above its default n_max, or resident ∞ moving more than one ladder step
predictions.note: SBX scales with 1/r: r(7200) = 0.0115 vs r(1800) = 0.01744 calls/s/session, so N_cpu ≈ [70.66, 79.49] → ladder [64, 64] at the same per-call cost. Resident ∞ holds one VM per session whatever the gaps, so its memory bound (≈ [51.41, 123.8]) does not move. CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: resident ∞ is expected to be CPU-bound here (see 1-2), and its CPU bound also scales with 1/r, ≈ [74.81, 84.16] → ladder [48, 80] at H = 7200 s, so the 'resident ∞ stays within one step' half is expected to be falsified unless memory binds first.

predictions.claim: Removing host-infrastructure sessions and chains moves both arms the same way. Neither point reverses the default result.
predictions.metric: sign of n_max(SBX) − n_max(resident ∞) at the no-infra and no-chains points vs the default
predictions.falsifiedBy: the sign at no-infra or no-chains opposite to the default point's
predictions.note: Direction fixed by SPEC §11; no numeric range (the points start two steps below each default N_max).

predictions.claim: The driver uses less than 1% of host CPU at every N (A2).
METHOD, NOT A PREDICTION: the two verdicts reported per arm and point, fixed before measurement.
predictions.note: Both verdicts use SPEC §8 conditions 1-2 unchanged, a class-matched pace condition (a session's expected time = the driver's schedule re-simulated over its window calls with each call's duration lengthened by its class's N=1 probe median added latency M[class], each send at max(previous send + the call's recorded offset, previous end), offsets joined from the corpus by trace and call index -- a join miss refuses the rung; class pace = observed / expected − 1; condition 3 = median class pace ≤ 0.10; the N=1 rung skips it and reports its raw median pace) and a class-matched condition 4. A call's excess = its added latency − M[class], M = the median added latency of its class in the arm's per-class N=1 probe (each class alone on an idle worker, 20 calls drawn from the class's corpus distribution; baseline.json class_medians). B = the probe's own within-class excess p95. n_max (PRIMARY): the largest ladder N that holds, every smaller rung holding, with condition 4 = p95(excess) ≤ max(3 × B, 50 ms). n_max_abs (secondary): the same, with condition 4 = p95(excess) ≤ B + 250 ms. The ladder climbs while either is unbroken and stops at the first rung where both fail. Per arm (B; primary limit; absolute limit; N=1 per-call overhead, information only): sbx B 229.2 ms, limit 687.5 ms, abs limit 479.2 ms, overhead 186.2 ms; resident-inf B 284.3 ms, limit 852.8 ms, abs limit 534.3 ms, overhead -15.83 ms; resident-300 B 290.5 ms, limit 871.4 ms, abs limit 540.5 ms, overhead -19.38 ms. Predictions 2-4 and 8 are stated against n_max.

predictions.claim: The metal rig shows the largest SBX gain: on the metal run, SBX's N_max ÷ resident ∞'s N_max is larger than on this nested instance.
predictions.metric: n_max(SBX) / n_max(resident ∞) at the default point, metal run (SPEC §13) vs this preliminary run
predictions.falsifiedBy: a metal ratio no larger than the preliminary one
predictions.note: Added by user decision after calibration, before the first measured rung. The metal run is on an AWS m7i.metal-24xl (SPEC §13; no nesting, 96 vCPU, EBS-only). Basis: SPEC §4 -- nesting raises SBX's per-Exec lifecycle cost (E10: resume 2.74×, destroy 5.56×) while the resident arm pays it once per session. Here the SBX lifecycle cost per call: direct no-op bench 0.09911 core-s per Exec; SBX − resident ∞ per-call CPU at N=8 = 0.2184 core-s.

predictions.claim: At mem512, resident ∞ is bound by memory and SBX holds more sessions than resident ∞. Predicted ranges: resident ∞ N_max in [8, 8]; SBX N_max in [16, 16].
predictions.metric: ladder.json n_max (primary) per arm at the mem512 point; record.json binding of each arm's first failed mem512 rung (with e15.slice memory.events high/oom for resident ∞)
predictions.falsifiedBy: resident ∞'s first failed mem512 rung not bound by memory (neither memory_floor, a memory-watchdog abort, nor e15.slice MemoryHigh throttling with Exec timeouts), or n_max(SBX) ≤ n_max(resident ∞) at mem512
predictions.note: Resident ∞: a VM keeps data.bin in its guest page cache, so it grows to near its 1024 MiB guest RAM: at N=8 the median VM is 951.1 MiB (max 1024). usable = MemAvailable at t0 1.2e+04 − 1536 floor − 1024 headroom = 9438 MiB; N = usable / footprint ∈ [9.217, 9.923] → ladder [8, 8]. Calibration smoke: N=8 holds (p95 excess 525.2 ≤ 861.6 ms); N=32 (with the 617ebb7 guards) does not: e15.slice was throttled at MemoryHigh (memory.events high 265,316), MemAvailable min 1427 MiB at t = 247.7 s (above the 1024 MiB watchdog floor, so no abort), VMs stalled into Exec timeouts -- the slice limit contained it (no global OOM), so record.py reads binding 'none', not memory_floor; this prediction counts MemoryHigh throttling as memory-bound. SBX: CPU 5.177 core-s/call × 0.01744 calls/s → N_cpu = [35.44, 39.87]. Disk: each SBX call of a scanning class (64% of calls) reads the 512 MiB dataset afresh, = 5.718 MiB/s per session; the host page cache serves those reads while the working set fits (per-inode cache: each session's data.bin is a distinct inode in its own workspace image, so caching does not share across sessions; about 11.63 GiB cache / 512 MiB ≈ 23.26 sessions), and past that the volume does (disk_read_max 130.5 MB/s ÷ 5.718 MiB/s ≈ 21.77 sessions). N_sbx = min(N_cpu, max(N_disk, N_cache)) = [23.26, 23.26] → ladder [16, 16]. Smoke: N=8 fails condition 4 narrowly (p95 excess 911.8 > 895.5 ms, a tail of ~7 of 135 calls; disk 3.909 MB/s mean); N=32 is disk-bound (130 MB/s mean, await 64.7 ms). CALIBRATION CONCERN, recorded before measurement: SBX's N=8 smoke did not hold, so n_max(SBX) may be 1 and the comparison may be a tie or reversed. Per-VM memory at mem512 includes host page cache for workspace.img (charged to the VM cgroup) and is not comparable with the default point's 74 MiB.
